options: A distant object's image forms close to this point → A diverging spherical mirror
A parallel reflected beam is used in reflectors → An object placed at the principal focal point
A dressing mirror → An object placed at the principal focal point
A parallel reflected beam is used in reflectors → A converging spherical mirror
questions.explanation: Object at the focus of a concave mirror — usual application or association: A parallel reflected beam is used in reflectors. Object at the focus of a concave mirror — optical description: An object placed at the principal focal point. Both parts must be correct.

questions.question: What happens to the image of a distant object when a concave mirror's upper half is covered?
options: A complete but dimmer image remains
The upper image half disappears
The lower image half disappears
No image forms
questions.explanation: Each uncovered part can reflect rays from the whole object; less light reduces brightness.

questions.question: An object moves towards a concave mirror from beyond C to between C and F. How does its real image change?
options: It moves closer and shrinks
It remains fixed at F
It becomes erect immediately
It moves farther from the mirror and enlarges
questions.explanation: The mirror equation predicts increasing image distance and magnification until the object reaches F.
